title: An intelligence ratchet locks evolution into improving cellular competency

fields.label: Label
fields.value: An intelligence ratchet locks evolution into improving cellular competency

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The authors suggest that because competency hides genetic deficiencies from selection, a positive-feedback ratchet arises in which evolution increasingly improves the problem-solving competency (intelligence) of its cellular material rather than the structural genome, a possible driver for scaling intelligence in morphological and other spaces.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Shreesha L 2023, Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model › 4. Discussion › 4.6. Where the Hard Work Is Done: An Intelligence Ratchet

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: This suggests the existence of a powerful ratchet mechanism in which evolution progressively becomes locked into improvements in the intelligence of the agential material with which it works, with reduced pressure on the structural genes.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Shreesha L, Levin M, “Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model”, Entropy (Basel, Switzerland) (2023), doi:10.3390/e25010131; section “4. Discussion › 4.6. Where the Hard Work Is Done: An Intelligence Ratchet”. Scope: Evolution of developmental systems; inferred from the 1D artificial embryogeny model

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-competency-13: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.42

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The minimal feedback can be tested in the public model, but the broad evolutionary and intelligence-scaling mechanism greatly exceeds that evidence. Existing data therefore resolve only a narrow model instance.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In diverse evolutionary models and biological lineages, test whether increased developmental repair reduces selection on structural loci and causes subsequent selection for still greater repair capacity. A repeatable lagged positive feedback would support the ratchet; scaling to intelligence needs separate measures.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Biological time-series evidence is lacking.

'Intelligence' is mapped to one restricted sorting operation.

The toy model does not establish ubiquity or long-term evolutionary lock-in.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.3
data existence: 0.46
analysis feasibility: 0.42
operationalizability: 0.52
discriminating power: 0.4

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The suggested ratchet is readable as a dynamical pattern in a public, fully specified toy evolution, so that pattern can be rerun. The claim then generalizes to an intelligence ratchet in developmental evolution and other spaces. Nothing public measures problem-solving competency and structural-gene selection jointly across real lineages, so only the model proxy is testable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In the 1D model, test whether hiding genotypic defects from selection produces a positive feedback in which competency keeps rising while structural-gene improvement stalls. That loop can be confirmed or refuted in the simulation. No existing dataset measures the same ratchet across real developmental systems or other problem spaces.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The model equates competency with bubble-sort steps on a monotonic axis, which is a narrow proxy for intelligence.

A positive feedback in this GA does not show a ratchet in evolving organisms.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.4
data adequacy: 0.32
data existence: 0.7
discriminating power: 0.28
analysis feasibility: 0.62
